titulo: Thirteen days of drift, nine named dates, and the month the island is yours
subtitulo: Easter here is reckoned on the Julian calendar and usually lands weeks away from yours; the compulsory holidays are a short list fixed by law; and July and January are two different countries
cena: The Thursday before an Easter your own calendar says already happened, and the baker is stacking flour like something large is coming.
frasePiso: Nine dates are fixed by name. Everything else you settle at the door: είστε ανοιχτά αύριο;

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Orthodox Easter is reckoned on the Julian calendar: the equinox is fixed at 21 March Julian, which is 3 April Gregorian, then the full moon, then the following Sunday, plus the rule that it may not fall before or together with Passover. The current drift between the two calendars is thirteen days. The two Easters coincided in 2025, on 20 April, and the next coincidence is 2028, on 16 April.
fatosDatados.fonte: Páscoa ortodoxa: calendário juliano, equinócio fixado em 21 de março juliano (= 3 de abril gregoriano), lua cheia, domingo seguinte, mais a regra de não cair antes nem junto do Pessach. Defasagem atual 13 dias. 2025 coincidiu (20 de abril); a próxima coincidência é 2028 (16 de abril). ⚠️ Mecanismo com confiança alta; lista de anos vem de tabelas de calendário, não da Εκκλησία της Ελλάδος.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Article 60 of Law 4808/2021 fixes the compulsory public holidays: 1 January, 6 January, 25 March, Easter Monday, 1 May, 15 August, 28 October, 25 December and 26 December. Good Friday is not on that list — it is a holiday for the public sector and for schools, while in the private sector it follows sector rules.
fatosDatados.fonte: O art. 60 da Lei 4808/2021 fixa as ημέρες υποχρεωτικής αργίας: 1/1, 6/1, 25/3, Segunda-feira de Páscoa, 1/5, 15/8, 28/10, 25/12 e 26/12 (Επιθεώρηση Εργασίας, hli.gov.gr). A Μεγάλη Παρασκευή NÃO está nessa lista.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Greece recorded 29.3 million international air arrivals in 2024, up 9.7 percent. July is the peak with 5.0 million, 16.9 percent of the total; January is the low with 648 thousand, 2.2 percent. The summer share, June to August, fell from 56 percent in 2019 to 50 percent in 2024, while spring rose 21 percent and winter 16 percent — the season is widening.
fatosDatados.fonte: INSETE, International Air Arrivals 2023-2024 (mar/2025): 29,3 M de chegadas aéreas internacionais em 2024 (+9,7%); julho é o pico com 5,0 M, 16,9% do total; janeiro é o mínimo com 648 mil, 2,2%. A participação do verão (jun-ago) caiu de 56% em 2019 para 50% em 2024, com primavera +21% e inverno +16%.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Sunday closing for shops was instituted in 1909, and already then it exempted restaurants, tavernas, patisseries, cafés and shops selling tourist goods — so what a visitor wants was never inside the rule. The current regime is article 16 of law 4177/2013, with declared exceptions and tourist zones set by ministerial decision.
fatosDatados.fonte: Domingo: fechamento instituído em 1909, já então com exceção para restaurantes, tavernas, confeitarias, cafés e lojas de artigo turístico. Regime atual: art. 16 do ν.4177/2013, com exceções (domingos de Natal, liquidações, 1º de maio e de novembro) e zonas turísticas por decisão ministerial. ⚠️ CONTESTADO: uma decisão de liberalização foi julgada inconstitucional; tema politicamente disputado.

steps.pt: Greece runs on two calendars at once, and the one that reshapes your week is not the one on your phone.
Easter here is reckoned on the Julian calendar. Thirteen days of drift, so it usually lands away from yours.

steps.acao: Two Easters, two dates. Check which one the week you booked is actually sitting next to.
steps.es: Φέτος το Πάσχα μας είναι δύο εβδομάδες μετά το δικό σας.
steps.pt: This year our Easter is two weeks after yours.
steps.tts: Φέτος το Πάσχα μας είναι δύο εβδομάδες μετά το δικό σας.

steps.pt: The two coincided in 2025, on the twentieth of April. The next time they meet is 2028.

steps.promptPt: A red date lands the next morning and this is the shop you need. Check with the counter before you plan it. Speak now.
steps.pt: Are you open tomorrow?

steps.acao: Take that as the answer for this door only. The place next to it decided separately.
steps.es: Αύριο είναι αργία, αλλά εμείς είμαστε ανοιχτά.
steps.pt: Tomorrow's a public holiday, but we're open.
steps.tts: Αύριο είναι αργία, αλλά εμείς είμαστε ανοιχτά.

steps.pt: Nine dates are compulsory holidays by name in law. Good Friday, surprisingly to most visitors, is not one.

steps.promptPt: The street feels quieter than a Wednesday should, and you want to know what the date is doing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Is tomorrow a public holiday?

steps.acao: That is the one date on the compulsory list that empties a town. Shop on the Saturday.
steps.es: Τη Δευτέρα του Πάσχα κλείνουν σχεδόν όλα.
steps.pt: On Easter Monday nearly everything closes.
steps.tts: Τη Δευτέρα του Πάσχα κλείνουν σχεδόν όλα.

steps.pt: Easter Monday is on the list, and it is the one that stops a whole town. Buy your food the Saturday before.

steps.promptPt: The shutter is down and there is a handwritten card taped to the glass that you cannot read. Ask a neighbour. Speak now.
steps.pt: When do you open again?
Then the second calendar: the season. July carries almost seventeen percent of the year's arrivals; January, two.

steps.promptPt: You are on the phone in November, thinking about a very quiet week two months out. Ask about the deep off-season. Speak now.
steps.es: Πόσο κάνει το δωμάτιο τον Ιανουάριο;
steps.pinyin: PO-so KA-ni to dho-MA-ti-o ton i-a-nu-A-ri-o
steps.pt: How much is the room in January?
steps.tts: Πόσο κάνει το δωμάτιο τον Ιανουάριο;

steps.acao: Cheap, empty and half shut all arrive together. Ask what is still running before you book it.
steps.es: Τον Ιανουάριο τα μισά μαγαζιά στο νησί είναι κλειστά.
steps.pt: In January half the places on the island are shut.
steps.tts: Τον Ιανουάριο τα μισά μαγαζιά στο νησί είναι κλειστά.

steps.pt: And the summer is shrinking. Its share fell from fifty-six percent to fifty, while spring and winter grew.

steps.promptPt: You liked this place and want the shoulder month instead of the crowded one. Put the request to the owner. Speak now.
steps.es: Μπορώ να κλείσω για τον Μάιο;
steps.pinyin: bo-RO na KLI-so ya ton MA-i-o
steps.pt: Can I book for May?
steps.tts: Μπορώ να κλείσω για τον Μάιο;

steps.pt: The fifteenth of August is a national holiday, and the largest pilgrimage of the year is on the island of Tinos.

steps.promptPt: You are planning around the biggest date of the Greek summer and you have left it late. Ask the guesthouse. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have a room on the fifteenth of August?

steps.acao: Boats and beds around that date go early. Book the crossing before you settle the room.
steps.pt: The fifteenth of August? Book tickets early.
Sunday closing dates from 1909 and always exempted the visitor's side: tavernas, cafés, shops selling to travellers.

steps.promptPt: Late afternoon on a holiday weekend, one errand left, and you would rather not cross town for nothing. Speak now.
steps.pt: Excuse me, what time do you close today?

steps.promptPt: Three shutters down in a row on the same pavement, and you still need the counter behind one of them. Ask a passer-by. Speak now.
steps.pt: I'm looking for a pharmacy that's open.

steps.promptPt: A stranger just saved you a pointless walk across town on a holiday. Close it warmly. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much, have a good day.

steps.es: Είστε ανοιχτά αύριο; Πότε ανοίγετε πάλι; Συγγνώμη, τι ώρα κλείνετε σήμερα;
steps.pinyin: I-ste a-nih-TA AV-ri-o · PO-te a-NI-ye-te PA-li · si-GHNO-mi, ti O-ra KLI-ne-te SI-me-ra
steps.pt: Shadow the three that cover any calendar: tomorrow, again, and until when.
steps.tts: Είστε ανοιχτά αύριο; Πότε ανοίγετε πάλι; Συγγνώμη, τι ώρα κλείνετε σήμερα;

steps.pt: A06 done. Thirteen days of drift, nine named dates, July against January, and one question at the door.

aprofundar.titulo: Two calendars, nine dates, and a season that is stretching

secoes.titulo: Why Easter moves away from yours
secoes.corpo: Orthodox Easter is worked out on the Julian calendar. The equinox is fixed at 21 March Julian, which is 3 April in the calendar on your phone; then the full moon; then the following Sunday; plus the rule that it may not fall before or together with Passover. The two calendars are thirteen days apart at present, which is why the dates usually sit weeks apart rather than on top of each other. They did coincide in 2025, on 20 April, and they meet again in 2028, on 16 April. Everything about your week — ferries, opening hours, whether a village has three hundred extra people in it — hangs on which of the two you are standing inside.

secoes.titulo: The nine that are fixed by name
secoes.corpo: Article 60 of law 4808/2021 lists the compulsory public holidays: 1 January, 6 January, 25 March, Easter Monday, 1 May, 15 August, 28 October, 25 December and 26 December. Nine dates, and Easter Monday is the moving one. The surprise for most visitors is what is not there: Good Friday. It is a holiday for the public sector and for schools, and in the private sector it follows sector rules rather than the compulsory list — which is why some shutters are down and others are not on a day that feels, from the street, like the most solemn of the year.

secoes.titulo: July and January are two different countries
secoes.corpo: Greece took 29.3 million international air arrivals in 2024. July alone was 5.0 million of them, 16.9 percent of the year; January was 648 thousand, 2.2 percent. That is a ratio of roughly eight to one between the same two islands in two different months. The useful part is what has been moving: the June-to-August share fell from 56 percent in 2019 to 50 percent in 2024, with spring up 21 percent and winter up 16 percent. The season is widening at both ends, which is exactly where the good weeks are. What nobody can tell you from a source is which specific island closes on which date — that varies radically between a large resort island and a small one, so the question belongs to the door, not to the statistics.

secoes.titulo: Sunday, and why it never applied to you
secoes.corpo: Sunday closing for shops goes back to 1909, and from the very beginning it exempted restaurants, tavernas, patisseries, cafés and shops selling tourist goods. In other words, the side of the economy a visitor actually uses was never inside the rule. The present regime is article 16 of law 4177/2013, with declared exceptions and tourist zones set by ministerial decision. It is worth knowing that this is live, contested ground — one liberalisation decision was struck down as unconstitutional — so treat any general claim about Sunday trading as unstable, and ask the specific shop.

secoes.titulo: The one question that beats every list
secoes.corpo: Είστε ανοιχτά αύριο, asked the evening before, is worth more than any holiday table you could memorise, because it resolves the one door you need rather than the country. Add πότε ανοίγετε πάλι when the answer is no, and τι ώρα κλείνετε σήμερα when the answer is yes but the afternoon is running out. Three sentences, and you never plan a day around a guess.

permissao: You are allowed to ask about opening hours as often as you like, in the plainest words you own, and you are allowed to be openly confused about which Easter is which. People who live there ask the same question constantly, precisely because the answer changes shop by shop and nobody expects a visitor to have worked out a Julian computus on the way from the airport.
espelho: Anyone who has driven across town on a bank holiday at home and found the car park empty already knows this shape. The only new part is that here two calendars are running side by side, so the trip you save is the one you asked about the evening before.

fichasCulturais.sinal: Your calendar says Easter was five weeks ago, and the town around you is only now filling with candles and closed shutters.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I have got my dates wrong, or this is some regional variation nobody told me about.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Orthodox Easter is reckoned on the Julian calendar — equinox fixed at 21 March Julian, then the full moon, then the following Sunday, with the rule about Passover on top. The calendars are thirteen days apart, so the two dates usually land weeks away from each other. They coincided in 2025 and meet again in 2028.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Look up the Greek date before you book, not the one you grew up with, and treat the Saturday before Easter Monday as your last full shopping day.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop being ambushed by the single busiest travel week of the Greek year, and you get to see it on purpose instead of through a train window.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: The thirteen-day drift is a calendar mechanism, not a fixed offset between the two Easters — the gap between them varies year to year and sometimes vanishes. Look up the actual date rather than adding thirteen days to your own.

fichasCulturais.sinal: It is Good Friday, the day feels like the most solemn of the year, and the supermarket on the corner is open.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Somebody is working a day they are not supposed to, or I have misread which day this is.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Article 60 of law 4808/2021 fixes nine compulsory public holidays, and Good Friday is not among them. It is a holiday for the public sector and for schools; in the private sector it follows sector rules. So the shutters go down unevenly, one decision at a time.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask the specific door about the specific day — είστε ανοιχτά αύριο — and save the hard planning for Easter Monday, which is on the compulsory list.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop writing off a whole week as closed, and you stop being surprised on the one date that really does stop.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Open does not mean ordinary. Services run through the evening, plenty of businesses close by their own choice, and in a small village the practical result can look exactly like a full holiday even though no law requires it.
